properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chesapeake Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-10
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 876308
Permit API: 015-20792
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Orwell Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-02-10
Comments: The DEP completed an administrative inspection on Chesapeake's Frisbee well site located in Orwell Township, Bradford County on 2/10/2020. The administrative inspection was completed in response to sample results 0983-078 received on 2/7/2020. The sample was collected for SAC 942 + Al, Br & Li on 1/14/2020 from pooled water located in front of the produced water offload area. The pooled water had a field measured conductivity of ~5.46mS/cm. Violations were cited as pending in inspection report #2983062. The constituents from sample 0983-078 that are elevated above normal concentrations you might expect to find in a stormwater puddle on the pad surface are as follows: Aluminum was reported at 8.033 mg/L Barium was reported at 21.48 mg/L Bromide was reported at 14.790 mg/L Iron was reported at 2.393 mg/L Lithium was reported at 1.788 mg/L Specific conductance was reported at 5320 umhos/cm Strontium was reported at 52.02 mg/L Chloride was reported at 1746.3 mg/L Based on the findings observed on location on 1/14/2020 and sample results 0983-078, violations cited as pending are now cited against API # 015-20792. The violations cited are as follows: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301

Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to IR 2997935 conducted on 2/14/2020 in which violations were issued. The entirety of the site was walked due to a pad lock on the gate (Photo 2). The access road still appears to be rutted which in several locations has allowed for the creation of accelerated erosion channels (Photo 1, 6, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17, & 27). Straw bale barriers still appear to be installed incorrectly and not properly maintained (Photo 4, 5, 9, 10, 14, 15, 18, & 19). The access road is still pooling water at low spots, this has created the potential for sediment discharges leaving the site (Photo 3, 8, 14, 18). In several locations the water has been standing long enough for tad poles to occupy them (Photo 20). No E&S Plan was found on site. Per the E&S Plan received in the operator's response dated 2/24/2020 and created in 2006, it appears that at least one culvert that was installed is not depicted on their plan, nor is it installed to the details set forth in that E&S Plan (Photo 7). Per 102.4(b)8 the E&S Plan must be available for review at the project site during all stages of earth disturbance activity. The access road and well pad do not have adequate temporary stabilization, nor have they achieved a minimum uniform 70% vegetative cover (Photo 1, 8, 11, 12, 13, 16, 22, 24, & 25). Down slope controls at the well site, do not appear to have been installed (Photo 23). Based on this inspection, violations will be issued as reoccurring for potential for discharge, and failure to have the site temporary stabilized, additional violations will remain outstanding.

Comments: On March 2, 2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill at the Marchezak John well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Accompanying the Department during this inspection are Range Resources representatives Denny Furmanek and Kevin Rudd. According to the spill report, approximately 25 gallons of diesel fuel were released to the surface of the well pad on February 28, 2026, at 9:30 PM.Prior to starting this inspection, the Department spoke via phone with Range Resources representative Derek Zofchak, who explained that the release occurred when a fuel truck experienced a fuel line failure while filling an on-site storage tank. Zofchak reported that remediation was completed on the day the release occurred, and that impacted material was placed in a rolloff dumpster on site.An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 11/20/2017.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Containment plan, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are on site in the mailbox (photos 3-6). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Setup of on-site secondary containment is not yet complete. However, Furmanek had the Containment inspection log available during this inspection (photo 15). The drill permits are on site in the company trailer (photo 16).The location where the 2/28/2026 diesel spill occurred appears to be freshly backfilled with stone (photo 7). No evidence of spilled diesel fuel, such as staining, odor, or a rainbow sheen was observed in this location. The fuel storage tank is placed within secondary containment (photo 8). A rolloff box is on site which reportedly contains the impacted material (photo 13). Rudd and Furmanek explained that air drilling operations have been completed. Drilling operations are expected to continue on the day of this inspection (photo 14). Four gas wells are planned to be drilled during this project. Five gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production. The GPU units and Dehy unit are not equipped with secondary containment (photos 9 and 10). However, the producing wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 12). All other storage containers and machinery on site that appear to contain regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photo 11). The secondary containments on site appear to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no observable holes or tears.The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 14). Furmanek explained that the well pad was expanded adjacent to the production tanks to better accommodate vehicle traffic for drilling and stimulation operation (photo 13). This location will be assessed in a future inspection, as further review is needed.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be noted and immediately corrected against the 2/28/2026 diesel fuel release.Transmittal of this inspection report was delayed due to an IT Error.

Drilling operations are expected to continue on the day of this inspection (photo 14). Four gas wells are planned to be drilled during this project. Five gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production. The GPU units and Dehy unit are not equipped with secondary containment (photos 9 and 10). However, the producing wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 12). All other storage containers and machinery on site that appear to contain regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photo 11). The secondary containments on site appear to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no observable holes or tears.The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 14). Furmanek explained that the well pad was expanded adjacent to the production tanks to better accommodate vehicle traffic for drilling and stimulation operation (photo 13). properties.content:
Report Details

Permit API: 129-25206
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/17/2025
Comments: On March 17, 2025, the Department conducted a routine inspection. Well is tagged, but tag is broken and thus does not display API number. Other piece of the tag is not observed on site at this time. Well posting is not observed on site. Well is located behind a large trailer covered in tarp and sitting on a cement pad. It is not clear what type of trailer this is or what is under the tarp. Three tanks are observed on site.- The first tank (Photos 5-8) is labeled 'Water' and is closed top and appears to be closed off with a cap at a valve at the bottom of the tank. A well tag is affixed to this tank with the API number of a different well (129-25077)- The second tank (Photos 9-13) is open top with fluid inside, nearly filled to the top of the tank and appears to be closed off with a cap at the bottom of the tank. Fluid inside is unidentified, but is brown in color, possibly due to rusting inside.- The third tank (Photos 15-19) is open top on one end, is open at the bottom near the valve and is not holding fluid at this time.Specific conductivity was measured on site. Background readings are approximately around 200 uS. Reading near each of the tanks are also approximately around 200 uS. It does not appear as though a release has occurred on site at this time. No production equipment is observed on site at this time. Disconnected lines and piping is observed on site. Black and orange lines are observed to be disconnected from the well and appear to possibly be old gathering lines. Other piping is observed, which appears to be drilling equipment. Violations are being issued for failure to tag and post the well, in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). The Department recommends replacing the current well tag and adding the well posting requirements to the site.The Department requests information on each of the three tanks and the trailer on site, including identification, purpose, and if they are necessary for the production of the well. The Department recommends removing all equipment not necessary for production of the well from the site.The Department recommends the Operator maintain freeboard operations in the open top tanks in accordance with regulations under Chapter 78.56.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8265631
Permit API: 019-21494
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/20/2026
Comments: Melissa Breitenbach (XTO) called the Department on 02/19/2026 to report a release at the well site which occurred at approximately 3:30 PM that day during plugging. I visited the site on 02/20/2026 and met with George Winebark (Operations Supervisor) to gather additional information.Per Mr. Winebark, the release was the result of a valve failure during the circulation stage, which caused an estimated 10 barrels worth of fluid to be expelled. At the time a water truck was on site and managed to collect most of the water as it was being released, which prevented much of it from reaching the ground or spreading off of the pad. The affected area was approximately 15' long and concentrated along a narrow strip where the water flowed. In the attached photographs, the pink flags show the extent of the release per conductivity readings. The highest conductivity readings (> 3.0 mS/cm) were close to the plugging location, and Mr. Winebark attributes these to historical usage (a since-removed production tank) rather than the released fluid, which was largely freshwater. Off pad, readings peaked at 1.8 mS/cm and dropped to 0.035 mS/cm and below within a foot or two. The release does not appear to have traveled more than 5' off pad. There is a stream approximately 500' downslope of the well pad.A section of what appears to be silt fencing seemed to be overwhelmed near the area where the release flowed off pad. The Department recommends repairing or replacing the fencing to prevent future runoff from continuing downslope. Per Ms. Breitenbach, a consultant has been enlisted to assist with Act 2 clean-up, and plugging will continue through the following week. Reclamation and clean-up will begin following the completion of plugging.

Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. The completions operations have ceased on Pad B and the snubbing rigs and their associated equipment have been removed from the pad. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad B. A representative from Creston Environmental was present on location as well. A crew was working on installing the GPUs on the pad. Trenches were being dug for the flow lines which will run from the well heads to the GPUs on the west side of the pad. A large trench was present at the well heads. Some fluid was seeping into this trench from the fill material surrounding the well cellar for well B-11H. The electrical conductivity (EC) of this fluid was 2.45 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was sucking up this fluid during this inspection. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up any elevated EC fluid found on the pad surface or during excavation on the pad. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) was empty during this inspection. A work crew was beginning to disassemble the MASS during this inspection. The north central area of the well pad has been excavated. One area is a long horizontal area approximately two feet of the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid here was 3.35 to 5.41 mS/cm. Another excavated area is to the southwest. According to Mr. Subra, EQT believes that the produced fluid that had been released to this area flowed along an area that had previously been excavated in association with a release that occurred during drilling operations on the well pad. Mr. Subra also said that the northwest area of the well pad where clamshell boxes had led to a release in the dancefloor area has been fully excavated. Additional excavation would still need to occur in the north central area of the well pad as well as in the northeast corner of the pad where the MASS still is present, he also stated. The lined sump remains at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel.Violations remain outstanding for the reported release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad B.

SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: COPPERHEAD ENTERPRISES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/09/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8280935
Permit API: 083-47442
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/09/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to being notified by Chuck Rippey of Copperhead Enterprises on 7/8/26 of a crude oil spill due to a compromised subsurface gathering line located at the entrance of the spur road that accesses this conventional well. At the time of notification, according to Chuck, all wells on the lease had been shut in and containment measures were being placed throughout the impacted area.At the onset of this inspection, I met with Chuck who explained that the gathering line failed due to valves on the gathering lines at the tank battery unknowingly being closed by a suspected, unknown, third party prior to the lease being pumped on the afternoon of 7/8/26. It is estimated that the wells on the lease were pumping for 2-3 hours before the well tender drove towards this well and noticed the release at approximately 15:00. After ceasing production and shutting in the wells, Chuck reported the release to this WQSS via telephone.At the origin of the release, crude oil had sprayed onto the road bank and lower limbs of nearby trees. The majority of the crude oil migrated west/ northwest in a roadside ditch alongside Chappel Fork Road for approximately 400' before reaching a spring run that evolves into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Chappel Fork. Pockets of crude oil were observed in the spring run/UNT between where it intersects Chappel Fork Road and its confluence with Chappel Fork. Crude oil was also present in an approximate 750' stretch of Chappel Fork downslope of the stream's confluence with the aforementioned spring run/UNT.At this time, underflow dams, absorbent booms and pads have been placed throughout the impacted portions of the roadside ditch, spring run/UNT and Chappel Fork to contain the released product. Crews were in the process of recovering crude that was collecting behind the various containment measures and replacing saturated absorbents as needed. I advised Chuck to continue the ongoing practices and to place additional booms in slow moving water to minimize the potential for further migration downstream. After further progress is made with recovering the free crude, Chuck intends to excavate the contaminated soil at the origin of the release and replace the ruptured portion of the gathering line.At this time, the quantity of crude oil that was released is unknown. Chuck intends to stage the excavated contaminated soil on a lined pod at this well site until proper disposal at a landfill is arranged. Documentation of this disposal and confirmatory sampling of the impacted area after its remediation is expected to be provided to the Department in order for this incident to be considered closed.Upcoming inspections will be done throughout the remediation of this release to ensure suitable progress is being made.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/16/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/16/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 948134
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2022
Comments: On March 16, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline and Brooke Millisock conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The DEP observed and sampled five seeps and four stream sites that were found off the west side of the well pad in "Deep Hollow" along an UNT to Rattlesnake Run. STL Resources revealed that the seeps were occurring and being monitored for specific conductivity and chlorides on March 1, 2022 during a meeting with the DEP. The data that STL Resources provided showed levels of elevated conductivity in seeps 1, 1A, and 4. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling site for pH and conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 had a pH of 8.61 and conductivity of 29.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 had pH of 7.97 and a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 had pH of 7.18 and a conductivity of 22.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 had a pH of 6.84 and a conductivity of 22.2. Seep 1 had a pH of 5.14 and a conductivity of 308 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a pH of 5.04 and a conductivity of 345 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a pH of 6.62 and a conductivity of 43.2 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a pH of 6.3 and a conductivity of 42.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a pH of 6.25 and a conductivity of 191.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had pH of 8.01 and a conductivity of 28.2 uS/cm. Water quality samples 0651-104, 106, 108, and 111 were collected at the four stream sampling sites and submitted for SAC code 942 plus Aluminum, Lithium, and Bromide. Water quality samples 0651-105, 107, 109, and 110 were collected at seeps 1,1A, 4, and 5. Water quality sample 0651-112 was collected in a channel downgradient of Seeps 2 and 3 due to not enough water available to sample in these seeps. An additional seep was observed up the logging road of Seep 3, this seep had pH of 6.67 and conductivity of 22.5. The previously mentioned seep did not appear to be monitored by STL Resources. The southwest infiltration berm excavation area remains uncovered and the stormwater level in the area as begun to recede eliminating the overflowing of the area. The water level in the southwest stormwater vault was about a foot deep and was unable to be screened for conductivity. The water level in the northwest stormwater vault was about 18 inches and could not be screened for conductivity. The seeps that were observed near the northwest stormwater vault on March 3, 2022 were not flowing at the time of inspection. A new area of excavation was observed where the water from these seeps was pooling. This area has been covered with a tarp. There was water pooled on top of the tarp and next to the tarp. The conductivity of this water was 3,400 uS/cm. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources said they will continue to vacuum the pooling water as necessary. The pooled water in this area could be seen overflowing into an adjacent depression that was covered with a tarp. The DEP recommends exploring this area and removing any contaminated water and soil. STL Resources has removed the contaminated soil stockpile that was being staged on the well pad. Well Pad remediation from the spill that occurred on January 8, 2022 has not occurred. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: At time of inspection, 41 degs. and cloudy. There are (4) wells on this pad. They are the Rosalie N 1H, N 3H, Rosalie S 1H and the Jack 8H, all were in production. The (9x5) and the (13x9) annulus vents are plumbed to surface w/2" pipe and T'd into a 2" common pipe venting to the prod. tanks. All annulus vents are open. The cellars had water in them w/ no bubbling observed during insp.. - On site today w/ well tender (Giovanni Dicupillo) to isolate the (13x9) annuli of the Rosalie S 1H, Rosalie N 3H and the Jack 8H and screen for gas due to gas being previously detected in the (13x9) annuli of these wells. The screenings were performed with an ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal.3/4/20). No gas was detected in the Rosalie S 1H or the Rosalie N 3H, however; gas was detected in the (13x9) annulus of the Jack 8H. Screening showed an LEL of 100% and a methane level of 4% at time of inspection. The gas meter was left on at well heads to check for gas at cellars and during walk around pad and prod. equipment. No gas was detected in ambient air. - Individual well pressures listed below were all taken off digital SCADA gauges. - N 1H - prod. tree top press.: 984 psi., prod. csg. press.: 1,026 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 6 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 1.7 psi., and prod. line press.: 975.2 psi. - N 3H - prod. tree top press.: 985 psi., prod. csg. press.: 786 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 4.0 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 3.0 psi., and prod. line press.: 973.6 psi. - S 1H - prod. tree top press.: 974 psi., prod. csg. press.: 1,014 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 4 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 5 psi., and prod. line press.: 972 psi. - Jack 8H - prod. tree top press.: 973 psi., prod. csg. press.: 1,025 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 4.0psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 4.0 psi., and prod. line press.: 967 psi. - There is self contained ancillary equipment on the pad. - There are (2) open well slots on the pad. - No obvious concerns or new violations noted. - Due to gas being detected in the (13x9) annulus, an FUI (Follow Up Inspection) will need to be scheduled to screen (13x9) annulus for gas again in the near future. Please contact OGI Eric Miller via e-mail at ertmille@pa.gov for scheduling of inspection.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/19/2025 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Richmond Township, Tioga county. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/18/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8249154
Permit API: 117-22252
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Richmond Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2025
Comments: On 9/19/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident/response to accident or event inspection at the Seneca Bechtel 674 well pad in Richmond TWP, Tioga County. This is in response to CTS 392369, describing the release of 10 gallons of diesel to the pad; the report received by the department on 9/18/2025. It was 63 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. The Site Act 9 sign, emergency response plan and PPC plan were located at the entrance to the access road. When I arrived on site, I met Seneca's HSE coordinator, Doug Tomlinson, who described the event as follows: Crews were on site installing production pipelines under the surface of the pad. Excavated material was being removed from trenches where the pipelines were being installed. The material was loaded onto a dump truck that was hauling the material to a stockpile on the northwest corner of the pad. While offloading the material onto the pile, workers believe that the front tire of the truck displaced a large rock that made contact with a pipe fitting on the side of the right diesel tank on the truck. This broke the fitting, the incident not noticed by the truck driver at that time. The driver drove approximately 300 feet from the pile of excavated material to the area where he was being loaded before somebody witnessed the diesel being released. The truck driver was stopped by a crew worker and the spill was contained. The release left a 300 foot path of spilled diesel that was approximately 8 inches wide with a larger pool where the truck stopped. The pipe fitting was on the fuel return line to the tank, The fitting has been repaired. The 300 feet of spilled material has been scraped up and loaded into a rolloff dumpster. The dumpster will be picked up by waste management and the material will be disposed when it has been properly characterized.The rock has been replaced along the 300 foot path but there was still a 10' x 10' area of the pad surface where the truck stopped that had not been filled in yet. While I was at the location, I did witness the dump truck offload excavated material onto the pile. Before the dump truck was allowed to drive on the pile to offload, a crew worker used an excavator to pack down the surface of the pile where the truck would drive. Pictures 10 through 14 were submitted by Seneca and show the impacted area, areas after being scraped, and the pad after clean stone was replaced.The pad is constructed to grade. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed around the site. Infiltration berms have been installed along the access road and the infiltration/MRC basin had been installed south of the pad. Most of the site is stabilized with at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation. Stabilization is becoming effective in recently disturbed areas. The temporary infiltration berm on the northwest corner of the pad has been removed. There are six wells permitted for the site at this time. The well cellars have been installed with the conductors scheduled to be installed on 9/22/2025. Current expectations for drilling is in 2026. The release of diesel fuel to the unprotected pad surface constitutes violations of these two regulations; SWMA 301 and CSL 402(b). The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends that Seneca personnel screen the area impacted by the release of diesel fuel for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Gas: 83 % (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened back to vent to production tanks @ 11:00. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the Cappucci Wyo 2H which is a (2) string well. **The presence of pressure and gas was also detected in the (20x13) annulus of the CAPPUCCI 4H. This is indicative of a violation of Title 25-chapter 78a.86 and 78a.85(a)5. The Department requests a response from Operator by 7/01/20 explaining how CALLC plans to comply with cited violations.

A leak was observed on the concrete below the pump jack (Photo# 10). A leak was observed on the concrete below the pump jack (Photo# 10). The Department recommends that the well equipment be inspected and the leaked substance be cleaned up to prevent further contamination at the site. Comments: On April 9, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation (CSE) at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows up to IR 4156824, where the violation issued in IR 4095466 for failure to comply with the 12/16/2021 CO and A was left outstanding. A Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) was executed between the Department and the operator on December 16, 2021. The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites." Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed during the inspection:The former well site appears to have overall established additional vegetative growth since the time of IR 4151340. However, it has not yet achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage. Additional temporary stabilization appears to be applied where vegetative growth has not yet occurred. What appear to be third-party vehicle tracks were observed at the former well pad location (photo 7). The Department recommends that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site.The super silt fence remains installed at the northern boundary of the former well site (photos 12 and 13). The operator reports that it pre-exists well site construction. The operator provided photos of the silt fence via email that were reportedly taken on 1/29/2026, and stated that the vegetative growth shown in the photos through the super silt fence could not have occurred since September of 2025; when the operator reportedly started site reclamation.No loose sediment was observed in the channel that empties into the Sediment Trap that reportedly pre-exists well site construction (photos 16 and 19).The Department recommends continued mulching and seeding of the former well site to establish adequate vegetative growth in the forthcoming spring.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4095466 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On August 6, 2024, the Department of Oil and Gas inspector, Cody Murray, conducted an onsite inspection of the HERBERT C SMITH 193D (Permit # 021-20852), operated by VESSELS COAL GAS INC.. • There is no visible well posting and no well tag ID on the well anywhere to be found. The hand written ID no longer legible. • The well appears to be not in use as it is disassembled in a few places. • The well valves are open to the pipeline and the surface is rusted entirely. • The well head appears intact with no signs of leaking. • OGI used an RKI GX-3R Pro to detect for the presence of gas and no gas was detected. • The 2023 annual production and mechanical assessment reports have not been submitted. • The most recent production report of 2019 indicated the well "Active" - Well Temporarily not producing. • The department requests the operator provide proof of production of the well and when it was last in use. Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess overall conditions on both pads. The drilling rig continues to operate on Pad B. I met with company man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on Pad B. Three small sumps have been installed in the pad surface since the previous inspection, in addition to the larger sump which had already been installed. All three are installed near the edge of the well site secondary containment and all three had stormwater in them during this inspection. One sump is on the north side of the pad not far from the original, larger sump. The electrical conductivity (EC) in this sump was 745 uS/cm. In the original sump the EC was 805 uS/cm. The sump on the east side of the pad, near the chemical tote storage area, was full of stormwater and the EC here was 718 uS/cm. The sump on the south side, closest to the company man trailer, had an EC of 516 uS/cm. The Department recommends continuing to pump out these sumps on an as-needed basis. No issues were noted on Pad B. On Pad A, multiple frac tank batteries remain on the pad within secondary containment. The wells are now fully staged for production. No issues noted on Pad A. Violations remain outstanding for the release on Pad B.
